note: Files this archive deliberately revised after materializing the pinned deployment. Every entry explains one difference from the historical pin in package.json. An entry is a reviewed change record, never a way to silence unexplained drift: a file that differs from both its historical pin and this list stays DRIFT.

revisions.name: contract.json
revisions.reason: Declare the P32D2 basic admission point in a separate basic_admission block, keeping the scale series prefills and decodes arrays unchanged so the 24 scale cases keep their identity, and add a display name per model so a receipt or a case id does not have to be read as a version string. Declare evidence_points: prefill 128 with decode 2 and 16 for qwen25_1p5b, the two points that have independent three-repeat NCU references. This reverses the earlier exclusion, which named P128D2 as an example of a pair that must be refused: the accepted evidence and the declared matrix could not both be right, and the evidence is what a run must reproduce. scale_series and basic_admission keep their axes, so the 26 existing cases keep their identity. Later revision: declare local_acceptance_matrix, the eight unique conditions of the local RTX 4000 Ada full-model traffic calibration. It is not a Cartesian product, so it states an explicit list of [prefill, decode] points and matrix_workload.py reads a block with points as exactly those pairs instead of as axes. Five of its points (P64D2, P256D2, P512D2, P128D4, P128D8) were undeclared before and were refused by the driver, so the acceptance set a local run was measured on could not be reproduced from this snapshot; the union of declared cases grows from 28 to 33 triples while the scale series, the basic admission point and the evidence points keep their identity and their counts. Declaring the points admits nothing and changes no gate.

revisions.name: matrix_workload.py
revisions.reason: Derive the case axes and the accepted (model, prefill, decode) triples from contract.json instead of a hard-coded tuple, so a declared point can actually be selected, and reject undeclared pairs such as P32D128 or P128D2. The accepted case now records its declared_matrix name. Derive the evidence_points block the same way as basic_admission, so declaring a point is what makes it selectable and an undeclared model in the block is refused. Later revision: read a declared block that carries points as exactly the [prefill, decode] pairs it lists, and keep the prefill/decode axes reading as the Cartesian product for the blocks that state axes. This is what lets local_acceptance_matrix declare a set that is not a product without inventing cases it does not hold, and it refuses a block that mixes points with axes instead of silently preferring one.

revisions.name: sample_pipeline.py
revisions.reason: Call matrix_workload.add_arguments instead of repeating the choice tuples, and validate the (model, prefill, decode) triple in the parent process. The duplicated gate is what previously rejected a declared point before it reached host.py; per-axis choices alone cannot see a pair such as P32D128, which would otherwise fail only inside the host child. Later revision: read SG_TEMPLATE_MODEL_POLICY, validate it against the adapter's own MODEL_POLICIES list, drop it from the child environment and pass it to the fitter as an explicit --model-policy. The stage environment is allow-listed, so the value travels in the job spec written by collect_case.py and the receipt records model_policy; the default stays strict, which is the policy every archived sample was taken with.

revisions.name: full_source_postprocess.py
revisions.reason: Take the projection policy from --model-policy instead of hard-coding strict, so a run can admit predicated global reads without forking the driver. The value is chosen from the adapter's own MODEL_POLICIES list, and the default keeps strict, so every archived sample stays reproducible. Refusing a predicated global read is what turns a weight-streaming class into an unfitted class, which is why this is a result-bearing parameter and not an implementation detail. The historical value is the imported snapshot file itself: this derivative is not covered by compact-sources/prepare.json, which records only the two cloned directories (observer, nvbit_sampler_r4/template_adapter_r4), and the import was byte-identical until this revision.

revisions.name: run_job.py
revisions.reason: Accept seconds = 0 as no wall-clock deadline. The replay entry documents that it has no deadline, so the controller must be able to express that instead of capping every job at 86400 s. Positive values keep the 1..86400 bound and the receipt records wall_clock_deadline.

revisions.name: followthrough.py
revisions.reason: Accept --model-uncovered and forward it to expand_profiles.py, and record the coverage of the expansion in the stage finish receipt before the memgen stage is allowed to run. Later revision: accept --engine and pass it to run_memgen.py as --binary. The cache stage used to be started with neither flag, so run_memgen.py fell back to its own machine-local default binary and the replay did not use the engine built from this repository`s source; collect_case.py builds that engine and now names it in job 2`s spec, exactly as its partial path already did. Without --engine the fallback is still available for old callers, but it now says so on stderr instead of being silent.
revisions.record: docs/EXPANSION_MECHANISM_AND_REFUSALS.md modeled completion section The same revision moves the frozen-engine build into followthrough.py as build_engine(target): the cache stage builds the binary from release/source/tools/ when it actually replays and names it with --binary, and collect_case.py imports that one function for its partial path instead of repeating the command. Before it, the replay named no binary at all and run_memgen.py fell back to a machine-local build this repository cannot hash.

revisions.name: profile_cache.py
revisions.reason: Same no-deadline fix for the cache stage, which killed the child at seconds + 60. --seconds is accepted and ignored. Later revision: accept --model-uncovered and forward it to expand_profiles.py. This entry's whole purpose is to expand a packed profile and replay it, and the flag decides whether a launch whose class has no admitted template is refused or given an explicit numeric_modeled profile; without it this path could only ever stop at the unsupported-profile gate and never hand the cache stage a full model.

revisions.name: expand_profiles.py
revisions.reason: Add --model-uncovered modeled, which completes a class with no admitted template as an explicit numeric_modeled object-volume profile (memgen-adapter/model_uncovered.py) instead of refusing its launches. The default stays refuse: a missing profile is still never a zero-traffic kernel. Modeled rows are counted separately (exact_launches, modeled_launches, modeled_fraction, modeled_by_cause), carry status PASS_MODELED_UNCOVERED_CLASS with model.target_addresses_hardware_observed false so the r4 original-allocation guard can still refuse them without a release re-pin, and the manifest now states fully_exact, exact_cross_layer_identity_claimed false and the HBServe-style not_claimed list. Later revision: also publish which evidence sized the modeled traffic (modeled_volume_basis with per-basis launch counts and per-CTA bytes, modeled_measured_bytes_per_cta, modeled_estimated_bytes_per_cta, modeled_estimated_share), so the share resting on the single run-wide bytes-per-instruction estimate is a recorded number and not something a reader has to re-derive. Later revision: attribute an ambiguous rule to the launch's own operand view. The context of a launch was walked up its parent modules, so an ancestor that inherited the same buffer contributed candidate views whose counterpart in the target layer lies elsewhere; the union of containing views then held more than one delta and the target was refused even though the kernel's own operand was not in doubt. rebind() now keeps, when the containing views disagree, only the views reached in the fewest call hops and requires their delta to be unique, refusing the rule when it is not, so nothing is guessed. Measured on the archived P32D2 sample with no new GPU work: 35544 ambiguous rules resolve, every one of them at hop 0, while 548718 already-unique rules keep their delta; the expansion moves from 1360 of 2060 packed launches to 1710, unsupported from 700 to 350, and every hardware-bound address of every binding that was already accepted is unchanged. The only addresses that move are the explicitly synthetic private-arena bases, whose run-wide cursor advances with the number of accepted bindings.

revisions.name: model_uncovered.py
revisions.reason: Prefer a measured width over the run-wide median when the run kept one. observed_lane_census() reads the refused records' own issue width in bytes per lane and the lane counts the projection censused them with, and per_cta_volume() carries that bytes-per-record figure to the class's classified records while the refusal covers at least OBSERVED_REFUSAL_COVERAGE_MIN of them; the basis is reported as observed_refusal_width_records_per_cta. Below that share the refusal describes a residue whose opcode mix differs from the bulk (a kernel refused for ten atomic lanes still has its loads), so the run median stays. Measured at P128D2 this moves ampere_bf16_s1688gemm_bf16_128x64_sliced1x2_ldg8_f2f_tn from 161792 to 621281 bytes per CTA, 3.84x, and the estimated share of modeled volume from 74.61% to 30.85%; P32D2 is unchanged because no class there clears the coverage floor. No claim about modeled rows changes: modeling.mode stays numeric_modeled, exact_cross_layer_identity_claimed stays false, and not_claimed is untouched.

revisions.name: run_memgen.py
revisions.reason: Carry the expansion coverage fields (modeled_completion, exact_launches, modeled_launches, modeled_fraction, modeled_by_cause, fully_exact) from the expanded manifest into the replay receipt, so a result that used modeled completion cannot be read as a fully exact stream.

claim_boundary: Producing a declared point is not an accuracy result and not an admission decision. validation/p32d2_branch_status.csv remains the authority for hardware-accuracy admission.
